title: MZ Attempting to create a simple cooking system

posts.author: JtotheK
posts.body:
Hello, everyone! I recently got RPG Maker MZ and am still learning the ropes, hoping to try and improve by making a simple idea into a working mini game. The idea here is to set up encounters and events where the player can gather ingredients before returning to their tavern to prepare and cook dishes that can be served to customers. I know I can set up a rather simple (if tedious) crafting system with conditional branches, but was wondering if there was any way I could set item attributes to ingredients that would be passed on to the final product. For example,
Raw Deer Meat (Savory: 2, Quality: 3)
Spicy Pepper (Spicy: 3, Quality: 1)
could combine into:
Spicy Deer Stew (Savory: 2, Spicy: 3, Quality: 2)
The idea is here that each customer would have a hidden taste profile where they like or dislike a dish depending on how close the dish's attributes match their taste profile.
If anyone has any better ideas to implement a cooking minigame as well though, feel free to suggest them!

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Regardless of how to do this, I don't think "simple" is the correct description here, haha. You're asking for independent items that take specific traits from the ingredients used. Nothing in this is simple. Especially not for a newbie.
You could of course go ahead and make conditional branches for every possible ingredient, saving their traits into variables and then making an end result item for every possible combination of traits and picking the right one as the result, but that is beyond tedious to do, so I would suggest investing in commissioning a coder to create a plugin that can do what you need.
That way you could have notetags, listing the traits of any given ingredient, randomize them even, and have the end result be a culmination of said traits. Doing this with eventing alone does not seem feasible to me.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body: Do the "trait values" vary within the same item? You don't need independent items if the base items always have the same "trait values". You can google for a free crafting plugin and then make recipes with that. Then just show the "traits" in the item info with icon-number pairs or whatever.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body: True, if it's fixed like that, pretty much any crafting plugin will work since the traits are more of less just smoke and mirrors.

posts.author: JtotheK
posts.body:
Yeah, after some digging around, I realized that this would be far more complex that I initially assumed, and commissioning a plugin would be counteractive to me learning.
I was instead thinking of perhaps using the choice function to allow players to choose specific ingredients (i.e Boar Meat, Deer Meat, Rabbit Meat and then Wild Greens, Farmed Vegetables, Exotic Herbs) with each one being assigned a Quality variable that would be added together to give the player a specific dish at certain Quality values (i.e Quality =< 3 Stew, Quality >= 4 Good Stew).
Still a bit tedious, but not as bad as making conditional branches for each possible combination. Would this be a decent alternative or is there a better way I could implement something like this?
